summary: L1 opacity is a derived state of layout-hiding field visibility rather than a distinct type-system primitive.

The implemented visibility model supports only transparent and fully opaque endpoints; mixed or partial field visibility is rejected pending a later offset-versus-accessor decision.
Enum visibility is all-or-none: per-variant visibility is not part of the opaque-export model.
The grouped source form `export opaque { T, ... }` exports nominal names while hiding all of their fields or variants.
Importers may name, hold, pass, and return pointers to an opaque nominal, but operations requiring its hidden layout—field access, dereference, construction, allocation, or by-value use—are rejected.

L1 defines separate constant-expression domains for array bounds, case arms, const initializers, and serialized interface constants instead of one universal constexpr rule.

summary: Dependency records retain their syntax but store the provider module's whole fingerprint, and declaration records contain no hash fields or suffixes.

summary: Every module defines an external one-shot `void I4init(void)` that initializes only its own deferred top-level lets and never its dependencies.

Per-module output contains no process-level C `main`, dependency lifecycle calls, or argument initialization; a later wrapper owns the complete process sequence.
A canonical dotted module name maps to a slash-separated relative stem with sibling `.c`, `.o`, and `.l1m` artifacts.

summary: Each separately compiled Dea object embeds enough module identity, interface, import, lifecycle, and entry metadata for standalone validation without reopening `.l1m` files.
